title: Alibi and Verdict
premise: Xanthe Zhou, a night-shift dispatcher who has spent a lifetime listening to other people's emergencies, receives two letters: one from a dying stranger confessing to a thirty-year-old murder, and one, unsigned, promising that Xanthe will be next. Following the confession's thread into the city's old taxi guild, Xanthe discovers the murder was pinned on an innocent driver—whose orphaned child was quietly adopted into the very family that framed him. As Xanthe closes in, they learn the confessing stranger is their own biological parent and the killer is still protected by the guild's surviving founders. In the end, Xanthe trades their hard-won invisibility for testimony, dismantling the alibi in open court and choosing the found family of fellow night workers over the blood family that lied.
about_author: Ulyana Joubert is a former court stenographer who spent eleven years transcribing testimonies before turning to fiction full-time. She writes mysteries about people whose jobs let them witness everything and be seen by no one.

chapters.title: The Night Frequency
chapters.summary: Xanthe Zhou works the graveyard shift at Meridian Taxi dispatch, invisible behind a headset, mapping the city through voices. POV: Xanthe. When two letters arrive in the same mail drop—one confessing to a murder, one promising more—the emotional beat is a cold jolt: someone out there knows Xanthe exists.

chapters.title: Confession, Then Promise
chapters.summary: Xanthe reads both letters repeatedly. The confession names the 1994 killing of driver Elias Okonkwo and claims the real killer walked free. The second letter is typed, unsigned, addressed by name. POV: Xanthe. Beat: dread sharpening into resolve as Xanthe decides not to hand the letters to police—not yet.

chapters.title: The Guild Archive
chapters.summary: Xanthe visits the defunct taxi guild's records office and meets archivist Priya Raman, who remembers the Okonkwo case. POV: Xanthe with a Priya interlude. Beat: first ally; the archive reveals Elias had a daughter, placed for adoption after his conviction-era disgrace.

chapters.title: Voices on Tape
chapters.summary: Priya plays a 1994 dispatch recording: Elias's last call, cut mid-sentence. Xanthe recognizes the dispatcher's cadence—it matches the confession letter's phrasing habits. POV: Xanthe. Beat: eerie intimacy across decades; Xanthe realizes the confessor once sat in their exact chair.

chapters.title: The Founders' Table
chapters.summary: Flashback chapter, 1994. Four guild founders meet over brandy the night after Elias's arrest, agreeing on a story. POV: founder Marguerite Voss. Beat: quiet corruption—decent people choosing self-preservation, and the alibi being built brick by brick.

chapters.title: A Name in the Ledger
chapters.summary: Xanthe traces the adoption: Elias's daughter became Dana Whitlock, raised by the Voss family. POV: Xanthe. Beat: vertigo—the victim's child raised by the conspirators, identity itself revealed as something handed down and falsified.

chapters.title: Dana
chapters.summary: Xanthe approaches Dana, now a hospice nurse, without revealing why. Dana is warm, guarded, and mentions her adoptive mother Marguerite's recent stroke. POV: alternating Xanthe/Dana. Beat: tentative connection; two lonely people circling a shared wound neither can name yet.

chapters.title: Second Letter
chapters.summary: A third letter arrives, this time describing Xanthe's apartment in detail. Police detective Amara Osei is assigned; she is skeptical but honest. POV: Xanthe. Beat: fear becomes physical; Xanthe must decide how much truth to give Osei while keeping the confession hidden.

chapters.title: What Marguerite Remembers
chapters.summary: Xanthe visits the stroke-slowed Marguerite Voss under a pretext. Marguerite mistakes Xanthe for someone named 'Ren.' POV: Marguerite fragment then Xanthe. Beat: pity tangled with suspicion—who is Ren, and why does Marguerite look at Xanthe like a ghost?

chapters.title: Ren
chapters.summary: Priya finds the name: Laurent 'Ren' Zhou, a guild dispatcher who vanished in 1995 after Elias's trial collapsed. Birth records confirm Ren is Xanthe's absent parent. POV: Xanthe. Beat: identity upheaval—the confession writer may be family; the promise-letter sender may know it too.

chapters.title: The Alibi That Held
chapters.summary: Reconstruction chapter: how four witnesses synchronized watches, swapped coats, and buried a cab's dashcam tape. POV: rotating founders. Beat: mechanical horror of conspiracy—each small lie reasonable, the sum lethal.

chapters.title: Night Shift, Watched
chapters.summary: Someone sits in a parked cab outside dispatch all night. Xanthe routes fake calls to shake them; coworker Theo covers without questions asked. POV: Xanthe. Beat: found family solidifying—the night crew becomes Xanthe's protective circle.

chapters.title: Osei's Cold File
chapters.summary: Detective Osei reopens the Okonkwo file independently and finds the same coat-swap anomaly Xanthe did. She confronts Xanthe about the letters. POV: Osei. Beat: uneasy alliance—truth offered in fragments, trust extended cautiously.

chapters.title: Dana's Doubt
chapters.summary: Dana discovers her adoption papers were backdated and her father's name altered. She comes to Xanthe, furious and shaking. POV: Dana. Beat: grief and rage; the two realize their investigations are the same investigation.

chapters.title: The Confessor Speaks
chapters.summary: Using the guild's old radio band, Xanthe broadcasts a message only a former dispatcher would monitor. Ren calls from a payphone: he confessed because he is dying, and he saw who killed Elias—but his own testimony was discredited long ago. POV: Xanthe. Beat: heartbreak; the parent is real, flawed, and nearly out of time.

chapters.title: Who Promised More
chapters.summary: Cross-referencing handwriting and shift logs, Xanthe identifies the threat-letter writer: sitting founder Casimir Hale, protecting the last living co-conspirator—himself. POV: Xanthe. Beat: cold clarity; the antagonist has been watching Xanthe since letter one.

chapters.title: Marguerite's Tape
chapters.summary: Dana finds a dictaphone cassette in her mother's effects: Marguerite, lucid before the stroke, naming Hale and describing the dashcam tape's hiding place. POV: Dana. Beat: bittersweet—a mother's partial amends, delivered too late for warmth but just in time for justice.

chapters.title: The Hiding Place
chapters.summary: Xanthe, Dana, Theo, and Priya retrieve the 1994 dashcam tape from a decommissioned cab in a guild-owned garage—and find Hale waiting. POV: Xanthe. Beat: terror and defiance; outnumbered, they record Hale's veiled threats on a live dispatch line.

chapters.title: Running Out of Time
chapters.summary: Hale accelerates: Ren is hospitalized under suspicious circumstances, and Osei is pressured to close the case. Xanthe goes public with the recording, burning their anonymity forever. POV: Xanthe. Beat: sacrifice—invisibility traded deliberately for voice.

chapters.title: Verdict Day
chapters.summary: Climax. Ren, from his hospital bed, testifies via video; the restored dashcam tape plays; Marguerite's cassette corroborates. Hale's alibi collapses under the synchronized-watch timeline. POV: courtroom omniscience anchored to Xanthe. Beat: catharsis—thirty years of silence broken in ninety minutes.

chapters.title: Elias's Daughter
chapters.summary: Dana petitions to restore her birth name; at the courthouse steps she asks Xanthe to stand with her as family. POV: Dana. Beat: tenderness—found family formalized not by paper but by choice.

chapters.title: Dispatch, Still Open
chapters.summary: Weeks later, Xanthe returns to the night shift, letters framed above the console. Ren visits in a wheelchair; the city hums on the board. POV: Xanthe. Beat: quiet resolution—Xanthe answers the next call, no longer invisible, no longer alone.
